why: The pilot's thesis from log 002 (2026-10-20): a wheel is a finisher dropped onto Brallin or Shabraz, never early tempo, and the deck runs too many of them. The champion, flown by his policy (hold every wheel until a commander is out), reads 0.797 on finisher wheel by T8; 0.82 is the nearest line the grading run can resolve. THE OBJECTIVE IS A GUARD, NOT THE VERDICT. The pre-registered profile, judged as a whole table and then at his table: dead wheels in hand @T5 DOWN; kept hand passes the pilot's keep rule UP; hand can act by T3 up or flat; both commanders out by T6 flat or up; extra cards by T8 and killed by T10 must not fall by more than their MDE; stall flat; wheels cast by T10 reported with no direction. Candidates come slot by slot with the pilot: of the eighteen wheel-shaped cards, the ones that also DO something and the repeatables on bodies hold their value, a bare seven-for-seven only Shabraz pays is the first to question; freed slots go to bodies, ramp or cheap draw. Torbran and Marauding Mako are keeps. Damage by turn X is not the question.
